notes: Sourced from the official Shure AD4D User Guide (pubs.shure.com/view/guide/AD4D/en-US.pdf), which includes a labeled rear-panel and front-panel diagram — the most authoritative and complete source found. The AD4D is a 2-channel (dual receiver) unit: each of the two channels has its own XLR and 1/4in analog outputs, while a single "AES3 1&2" XLR-type connector carries the AES3 digital output for both channels. Ethernet: the unit has 4 RJ45 ports (ctrl1, ctrl2, Dante Primary, Dante Secondary) supporting 10/100Mbps or 1Gbps depending on mode (Split-Redundant: 2 ctrl + 2 Dante; Switched: all 4 ports carry both). AES3 connector on the rear panel is drawn as a 3-pin XLR-type connector per the official wiring diagram (not a standard analog XLR, but physically the same 3-pin XLR form factor) — labeled here as xlr3 since that's the closest connector type in the given list. Antenna, RF cascade, and word clock connectors are all BNC. Power input is an IEC locking connector (not a standard IEC C13/14 - it's Shure's proprietary "VLock" locking IEC-style connector), rated 100-240V AC. An optional AD4D-DC power module variant exists supporting redundant DC power (10.9-14.8V DC, 3.3A max) as an internal add-on module rather than a distinct rear-panel port on the base AD4D — this DC input was not included as a separate port since it's an optional accessory module, not a standard connector on the base unit. Grades were only set on RJ45 Ethernet ports (eth-1g, since the network interface spec explicitly states 10/100Mbps and 1Gbps support) — no grade applies to BNC (RF/word clock, not video/SDI), XLR/TRS (analog/AES3 audio, not USB/HDMI/DP), or IEC (power) connectors per the grading rules.
